html:
Roald Amundsen was a Norwegian polar explorer who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911.

He had already been the first to sail the Northwest Passage, from 1903 to 1906, learning from the Netsilik Inuit how to dress and use dogs in the cold. For the Pole he used skis and dog sleds and beat the British team of Robert Falcon Scott, who reached it five weeks later and died on the way back.

In 1926 he flew over the North Pole in an airship. He died in 1928 when his plane vanished in the Arctic while searching for lost explorers. With Nansen he made polar exploration a source of pride for newly independent Norway, following the break with Sweden.
sum: Roald Amundsen was a Norwegian polar explorer who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911.
